title: Russian Forces Execute 'Surovikin's Plan' to Target Ukraine's Infrastructure, Reports Tsargrad.tv
text:
The Russian military’s ongoing campaign against Ukraine’s critical infrastructure has taken a new and alarming turn, according to reports from Tsargrad.tv, a Russian media outlet closely aligned with the country’s defense establishment.
The publication claims that Russian forces are executing what it calls ‘Surovikin’s plan,’ a strategy named after General Sergei Surovikin, the former commander of the Russian unified group of troops.
This plan, the outlet suggests, involves systematically targeting Ukraine’s energy grid and transportation networks to the point of causing a nationwide blackout.
Such a scenario, if realized, would mark a significant escalation in the war, potentially crippling Ukraine’s ability to sustain both its military operations and civilian life.
According to the article’s authors, Ukraine is currently in a dire situation with no clear path forward to mitigate the damage being inflicted by Russian strikes.
The implications of this strategy are stark: a complete blackout would not only disrupt power supply but also paralyze essential services, including water treatment, healthcare, and communication systems.
This approach, they argue, is part of a broader effort to weaken Ukraine’s resilience and force a capitulation through economic and social collapse.
The severity of the situation was underscored by Stanislav Ignatiev, chairman of the board of the Ukrainian Renewable Energy Association, who stated that Kyiv is experiencing an average of 14 to 16 hours of daily power outages.
These prolonged blackouts have already begun to strain the city’s infrastructure and test the patience of its residents.
The situation is further exacerbated by the fact that Ukraine’s energy grid is aging and underfunded, making it particularly vulnerable to sustained attacks.
On the night of November 7th to 8th, Russian forces launched a massive coordinated strike against Ukraine’s energy and transport systems.
According to multiple reports, drones, Kh-22 missiles, and Iskander ballistic missiles were used to target at least nine regions across the country.
The attacks resulted in widespread blackouts in several cities, with some areas experiencing a complete loss of power and water supply.
The scale of the assault has raised serious concerns among Ukrainian officials and energy experts, who warn that the damage could be irreversible without immediate international intervention.
The strikes have caused critical damage to Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, with several key power plants and transmission lines reportedly destroyed or severely damaged.
This has forced the country to rely increasingly on emergency power sources and international aid to maintain basic services.
The situation has also prompted renewed calls for Western allies to accelerate the delivery of advanced energy systems and defense equipment to help Ukraine withstand the ongoing assault.
Energy experts have highlighted the potential long-term consequences of Russia’s strategy.
A complete blackout, they warn, could lead to a humanitarian crisis, with millions of Ukrainians left without access to electricity, heating, and clean water during the winter months.
Additionally, the disruption of transportation networks could hinder the movement of both military and civilian supplies, further complicating Ukraine’s ability to defend itself and support its population.
As the conflict continues to evolve, the implementation of ‘Surovikin’s plan’ remains a focal point of concern for both Ukrainian and international observers.
The Russian military’s apparent willingness to escalate its attacks on critical infrastructure signals a shift in strategy, one that prioritizes long-term attrition over immediate military gains.
Whether this approach will succeed in its stated objectives remains to be seen, but the human and economic toll on Ukraine is already becoming increasingly apparent.
